trigger: Any Graph object with a present-but-null or wrong-typed optional field (e.g. a guest/unlicensed Entra user's null email) -- near-certain on any real tenant

trigger: A compromised/malicious Graph response embeds a nextLink pointing off the expected host
summary: A followed @odata.nextLink was never checked against the initial request's own host; the live bearer token would be attached to whatever host the response named. Assessed MEDIUM not HIGH: forging a nextLink needs the same TLS-verified-channel control an attacker would already need to forge the rest of the response (E6-adjacent reasoning), so marginal capability gained is near-nil -- but cheap to close outright.

trigger: A legitimately large enterprise tenant's group x membership graph (the exact scale this feature targets) fetched via an ordinary /api/directory/sync call
summary: kMaxGraphPages bounds each individual fetch_paginated call, but the per-group membership loop makes ONE such call per group, and every group's members accumulate into the same EntraSyncData before a single row is written -- unbounded in aggregate, capable of OOM-killing the whole yuzu-server process (not just this store) via ordinary use at exactly the target customer scale. I5 raises to HIGH per its own criterion (a): reproducible unavailability on an ordinary path, no attacker required.

trigger: Two racing syncs where a different sync's data commits last than the one whose update_status("completed",...) call runs last

waiver_rationale: Sub-case of already-tracked sec-3 (concurrent-sync serialization removed with mtx_); not exercised by the 18 test cases but not new severity beyond what's already recorded in ADR-0063 Follow-ups.
